newsitem.title: USA: American Exploration battles well blowout.
newsitem.headline: American Exploration battles well blowout.

text.p: Firefighters contracted by American Exploration Co on Wednesday were studying options to extinguish a fire sparked by a blowout on one of the company's platforms off the coast of Louisiana, officials said.

Divers closed off block valves on oil and gas lines to isolate the fire burning on a production platform and drilling rig over a cluster of wells about 100 miles southeast of Cameron, La., in East Cameron Block 328.
The blowout sent flames shooting 30 feet into the sky over several wells producing oil and natural gas in shallow waters of the Gulf of Mexico and 51 workers were evacuated safely.
The U.S. Coast Guard said a half-mile wide oil sheen stretched six miles from the platform and was dissipating. The natural gas-fed fire otherwise was not expected to cause environmental damage.

The fire was ignited by natural gas leaking from a four-inch pipeline aboard the platform, which was linked to a drilling rig operated by Pride Offshore, a unit of Pride Petroleum Services Inc, company officials said.
Houston-based American Exploration acquired the field last year and was producing 7 million cubic feet of natural gas and 350 barrels of oil per day.
